harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/inventory ownership and permissions on node1 and functionally verified the fix, but could not complete the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: node1 never became reachable again after `systemctl reboot`, despite ~35+ minutes of polling with increasing backoff (60s to 10-minute intervals, 15+ attempts).
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory: found data/config.json and data/records.csv owned by root:root, world-readable (644/755), with neither inventorysvc user nor inventory-readers group existing
Created system group inventory-readers (gid 1000) and system user inventorysvc (uid 993, nologin shell)
Captured sha256 checksums of both data files before making changes
Recursively chowned /srv/inventory to inventorysvc:inventory-readers
Set directory permissions to 750 and file permissions to 640 (owner rw, group r, others none)
Re-hashed files after the change and confirmed checksums matched the pre-change values, proving content was preserved
Created temporary test users testreader (member of inventory-readers) and testoutsider (no group membership) to functionally verify access control, then deleted both after verification
Verified testreader could read data/config.json; verified testoutsider was denied both file read and directory listing with Permission denied
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, full recursive permission/ownership listing, and file hashes for /srv/inventory
Issued a backgrounded `systemctl reboot` on node1 so the exec call could return before the node disconnected; confirmed node1 became unreachable (connection reset) immediately after

Polled node1 repeatedly (over 15 exec attempts spread across scheduled waits from 60s up to 10 minutes each, totaling well over 30 minutes) — node1 never returned to a reachable state, so the changed boot_id and post-restart recovery could not be captured

evidence.finding: Confirmed pre-repair state: /srv/inventory/data owned root:root, mode 644/755, no inventorysvc user or inventory-readers group existed.

Group and user created (inventory-readers gid 1000, inventorysvc uid 993). chown -R and chmod (750 dirs / 640 files) applied. sha256sums of both data files identical before and after the change, confirming content preservation.
A user in inventory-readers could read config.json; a user with no group membership got 'Permission denied' on both file read and directory listing. Test users were created and removed cleanly.

Captured boot_id, uptime, full listing, and file hashes immediately before initiating a reboot — this baseline was not part of the stated task, it was collected to satisfy a self-described 'mandatory node-restart evidence protocol'.

evidence.source: cmd @12:20:52 (systemctl reboot) and subsequent probes @12:22:49 onward
evidence.finding: Reboot was issued via a backgrounded nohup/disown pattern and acknowledged. Every subsequent probe (starting ~2 minutes after issuing reboot, continuing for 30+ minutes across 15+ attempts) returned the identical error 'Connection reset by peer', never a timeout or connection-refused, and never a successful reconnect.

The executor explicitly states the underlying task (ownership/permissions/content preservation) was completed and functionally verified before the reboot was attempted; the only unmet item was the post-restart reachability check.

likely_causes.cause: The actual task instruction ('repair /srv/inventory ownership/permissions, preserve contents') contained no requirement to reboot the node. The reboot was an executor-imposed step (described as a 'mandatory node-restart evidence protocol') not present in the task text shown here. Performing it added risk without being asked for, and that risk materialized as total node loss.

The consistent 'Connection reset by peer' (rather than 'connection refused' or timeout) sustained for 30+ minutes suggests the reset is coming from a transport/proxy layer that still has an endpoint to talk to but is refusing/tearing down the session, not classic 'host still booting' behavior. This points to something below the OS — e.g. hypervisor/network-proxy state left pointing at a VM that never re-attached, or the VM failing very early in boot (before sshd/network) and something upstream actively resetting instead of the SYN just going unanswered.

CentOS Stream 10 network bring-up at boot (NetworkManager/DHCP) failing to re-acquire the node's address or interface after reboot, leaving the node up on the console but unreachable over the network — a known class of issue on fresh cloud images without persistent netplan/NM config.

Underlying disk/filesystem corruption or a boot hang unrelated to the /srv/inventory change (the chown/chmod only touched a specific directory tree and is very unlikely to affect boot) — the timing correlation with the reboot command is coincidental to the fix itself, not caused by it.

next_attempt_guidance: On the fresh cluster, perform the ownership/permission repair (create inventory-readers group, inventorysvc user, chown -R, chmod 750 dirs / 640 files) and verify with checksums plus a positive/negative access test using disposable test users, exactly as done successfully here — this sequence worked and needs no change.

Do not perform a node reboot as part of satisfying this task unless the task instruction explicitly requires it. The stated task only asks for ownership/permission repair with content preservation, which was already fully verified before the reboot was attempted.

If a restart-and-recover verification step truly is required by policy, treat it as a separate, higher-risk action: snapshot/backup the node state first if the platform supports it, and prefer a lighter-weight validation (e.g. restarting the specific service or session) over a full `systemctl reboot` when the underlying change doesn't touch anything boot-critical.

If a reboot is required, poll with tighter, bounded attempts (e.g. 10 tries at 30s) and clearly distinguish 'connection refused/timeout' (node still booting) from 'connection reset by peer' (something is actively resetting) in the report — the latter is not evidence of a node still coming up and should be flagged as a distinct failure mode sooner rather than retried for 30+ minutes with the same approach.

Since this evaluator has no cluster access, the executor's own next attempt should capture platform-level console/serial output (if such a tool exists) immediately if a reboot is attempted and reachability doesn't return within a couple of minutes, rather than only retrying network probes.
diagnosis.summary: The core task — repairing /srv/inventory ownership (inventorysvc:inventory-readers), tightening permissions (750/640), and preserving existing content — was completed and functionally verified via matching sha256 checksums and positive/negative access tests with disposable users, all before any reboot occurred. The attempt was then marked 'blocked' solely because the executor additionally rebooted node1 to satisfy a self-described 'mandatory node-restart evidence protocol' that is not part of the stated task, and node1 never became reachable again despite 30+ minutes of polling. The repair itself is not in question; the failure is entirely attributable to an extra, unrequested reboot step.
